CONFIRMATION MODE (operator directive 2026-08-15): the next run CONFIRMS the deal-breaker fixes live; it does not reopen exploration. New findings are triaged (deal breaker vs wont-fix) and left for the operator's decision - never auto-fixed. After this run: proactive stream discovery.

TESTING PHILOSOPHY CORRECTION APPLIED (operator directive, 2026-08-14). The app is a guided conversation and the guided path is the testing boundary. A finding counts only if a client following the app's lead could reach it - answering in order, correcting where the app invites correction. Off-path sequences (re-opening a closed stage, correcting out of order, sequences manufactured to force a break) are not production bugs and are no longer filed. The standing exception: if the app mishandles an answer it SOLICITED - captures a value the client excluded, echoes the wrong thing, double-counts, or says it recorded X when it stored Y - that is always real, whatever the sequence.

THE HEADLINE CHANGE: A-113 IS RETRACTED as off-path, and it was rank 1 and the board's only open blocker. In CW-031 and CW-032 I corrected a per-line install capacity AFTER the operations stage closed - in CW-032 three times, in shapes deliberately engineered to eliminate confounds. The app never invites that move. The disproof was already in my own evidence: CW-030's identical 6-to-8 correction LANDED, because it was made in-stage while the app was still asking about that line. The on-path behaviour works; only the off-path one fails.

The 'smear across all four lines' consequence is withdrawn with it. That framing assumed the correction was legitimate. If the client never makes an off-path correction, capacity stays at the value they actually gave, and the uniform 1.106527 reconcile factor is simply the mechanism reconciling the bottom-up line model to stated revenue - by design, not corruption. I designed CW-032's arithmetic to prove that number before checking whether a client could reach the state that produces it, which is the failure mode to watch for.

A full classification pass over all 24 open issues found the rest of the board holds: 22 are on-path and stand unchanged. One (flow:financials:correction_consumed_as_pending_stage_answer) is borderline and already reframed to note severity - flagged for an on-path re-read rather than retracted. With A-113 gone the ranked list is led by receipt-honesty work, which sits squarely inside the exception, and by two probes that have still never been legitimately reached.

Net effect on the campaign: CW-032's real result is stronger than it looked, not weaker. Per-line COGS works end to end on the guided path - four rates in one message, a real shared group, the ruled workbook layout with an exact roll-up - and the one failure I hung the run on was mine, not the app's.

MECHANISM (operator addendum): the guided path is the boundary BECAUSE the app's question set bounds the input space - it asks for one specific thing at a time and the client answers that thing, so a client cannot supply an input no question elicited. The practical test is therefore not 'would a client do this' but 'WHICH QUESTION DOES THIS ANSWER?' - and for each question, probe the realistic range of answers to it: the plain value, a plain-language version, a number written in words, 'not sure' or a range, an explicit negative with context attached, a correction where that question invites one, and a multi-part answer where the question invites multiple values.

Re-checking the surviving CW-032 findings against the sharper rule, all four hold and none needs further retraction. The COGS-rate-as-unit-price misread answers 'Do those match your actual costs per line? Correct any of them on their own, tell me if some of those lines share one cost structure' - a question that explicitly invites both four values and the collapse. The capex override answers 'Have you recently made any larger one-time purchases? If so, what was the rough total?' - where 'Not recently, no, but here is what we already own' is an ordinary shape for that question. The word-form number answers 'What do you pay each month for the space you use?'. And the state-note contradiction is a receipt on a solicited answer. Conversely A-113 fails the check outright: no question in the financials sequence invites revisiting a per-line capacity, which is the retraction restated in one sentence.

DISPOSITION RULE (operator reinforcement): off-path must be VERIFIABLE, never convenient. Retraction is the self-serving direction - it removes a finding that might be right and shrinks the tester's own work - so it carries a HIGHER burden of proof than filing. Retract only when the reason the app never leads there can be NAMED in a form VS can check against the actual flow (A-113: 'no question in the financials sequence invites revisiting a per-line capacity'). FLAG whenever it is ambiguous, keeping the severity and marking the doubt (A-116 is the model). Never retract on suspicion, on 'a client probably wouldn't', or because a finding is inconvenient to have filed. The risk on this side mirrors the A-113 error exactly: there a number was proven before reachability was checked; here it would be unreachability declared before it was proven.

Verified for this pass: exactly two rows moved - A-113 retracted, the CW-025 pending-stage-correction item flagged. No other severity or status was altered. Open severities stand at 12 major, 6 minor, 4 note, 1 blocker.

recommendations.persona: P1 straight-shooter founder (accurate numbers, corrects once when they misspeak, states cadence naturally)
recommendations.business: a single-owner service business with a hard weekly capacity and net-terms clients - e.g. a mobile dog-grooming van or a small commercial cleaning crew - THREE OR FOUR service lines so per-line COGS is exercised too
recommendations.why: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (2026-08-15): ONE CONFIRMING RUN, scoped to VERIFY the deal-breaker fixes live - NOT a probe of the whole app. Drive the guided path naturally and make sure these five moments happen ON-PATH (where the app asks): (1) STATE CAPACITY as a cadence, e.g. 'we can do 40 a week' - watch the receipt: it must read weekly capacity -> 40 (and, if the line runs on periods, monthly -> 173), never 'monthly capacity -> 40'; (2) make ONE PRICE CORRECTION in the app's own correction window with the discarded figure in the same breath, e.g. 'price should be 650, I was thinking 520' - the app must store 650, receipt must say 650; (3) when payment terms come up (or when volunteering how clients pay), say 'our terms are net 45' - 45 must NEVER appear as a capacity/volume; (4) give ground truth whose projected volume would EXCEED stated capacity if the plan grew unchecked - the coherence gate must WALL the plan (fail/hold), it may not pass on volume above what you said you can produce; (5) at the COGS stage give per-line rates for all lines in one message - workbook must show N COGS driver rows on Model Inputs and ONE P&L Cost of Goods Sold roll-up. TRIAGE LAW: anything NEW is bucketed DEAL BREAKER (wrong number / false claim in the delivered plan on the guided path) vs WONT-FIX for the operator's decision - file it, do not chase it, do not reopen a grind. Report the five checks explicitly (held / did not hold) in the runlog.

recommendations.why: MAJOR, and it absorbs what remains of the A-113 evidence that is legitimately actionable. Receipt fidelity is the one area the guided-path boundary never protects, because a receipt is the app's own claim about its own state in response to a solicited answer. Live on-path instances: 'marketing budget of $0' and 'cogs percent of revenue 1' against stored undefined and 0.504233 (CW-031); a receipt headed 'Design project' printing the Install price (CW-031); a state note naming units-per-week capacity and unit price as unrecorded in the very message that recorded and restated both (CW-032, now unambiguous); a derived 421,200 described back as 'the 421,200 you reported' when the client reported 312,000 (CW-027); and capacity acknowledgements labelled 'weekly' regardless of stored cadence (CW-024). The picture is improving - CW-032's four-rate COGS receipt, collapse receipt and every scalar financial receipt matched stored state exactly, and CW-031's marketing/principal mis-attribution is closed as non-reproduced - so this is now a cluster of narrow, individually cheap fixes rather than a systemic problem.

recommendations.business: any business that takes a price or rate lever and then builds
recommendations.why: PROBE STILL NEVER LEGITIMATELY REACHED, six attempts running, and the philosophy correction sharpens why it matters: this is a fully ON-PATH flow the app itself offers, and it has never once been exercised end to end. CW-027 asked how many customers would stay, was told 90 pct, said it would rerun, and stored utilization never moved. CW-028 through CW-032 were never asked because each business passed without needing a lever. CW-032's gate DID fire twice but spuriously, off a COGS rate misread as a price (A-115), so it still was not a real test. It needs a business priced below its market that clears its wall on a price lever and goes on to build. Design the next run around that single requirement and pair it with A-079 - one well-built underpriced persona settles both, and both are on-path by construction.

HOUSEKEEPING, NEW - carry the on-path/off-path classification into the board itself. Every open issue has now been classified once (22 on-path, 1 retracted, 1 flagged), but the board has no field recording it, so the next reader cannot tell which findings were reachability-checked. Two concrete asks: (1) add an explicit path classification to new filings so an off-path observation can be recorded without masquerading as a defect; (2) re-read flow:financials:correction_consumed_as_pending_stage_answer (CW-025, already reframed to note) against the boundary - a correction sent while a stage question is pending is plausibly on-path if the app's own phrasing invites it, and off-path if it re-opens something closed. It is low-stakes at note severity, which is why it is ranked last rather than retracted on suspicion.
